method.label: Compare sum factors with the factorial

annotationRationale: The decisive step is prime-factor divisibility: the sum for n=996 contains the prime 997, which is absent from the factorial. The arithmetic-series formula and factorial notation support the comparison.
sourceMethod: Follows the official parity and prime-divisibility argument, specializing the composite case to n=998 and checking only the candidates needed to establish the greatest value.

review.mathCheck: Odd \(n>1\) works as a divisor case, excluding 999 and 997. For 998, the distinct factorial entries 499, 27 and 37 supply the entire sum. Trial division by every prime below 32 confirms 997 is prime, so \(498\cdot997\nmid996!\). Therefore 996 is the greatest qualifying value, choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution 9's parity and prime-obstruction method on page 5. Checking the three larger candidates replaces the official general even-case assertion and fully establishes maximality.
review.annotationCheck: Prime-factor divisibility is assessed; arithmetic-series summation and factorial notation support it. No successive-prime-power counting or factorial-valuation node is needed.
